'''''Laurencia''''' is a [[genus]] of [[red algae]] that grows in temperate and tropical shore areas, in [[Littoral zone|littoral]] to [[Littoral zone#Sublittoral zone|sublittoral]] habitats, at depths up to {{cvt|65|m}}.<ref name=algaebase/>

==Description==
{{Expand section|date=February 2016|small=no}}
''Laurencia'' species have a [[thallus]] that is erect or [[wikt:decumbent|decumbent]] with [[distichous]], whorled or radial branch arrangement.<ref name=algaebase/>

== Taxonomy and Nomenclature ==
The genus name of ''Laurencia'' is in honour of Louis Jean de La Laurencie (1768-1829), who was a French Naval officer, Director of the [[University of Limoges]] and also a friend of the author, [[Jean Vincent Félix Lamouroux]].<ref>{{cite book | last=Burkhardt | first=Lotte | title=Eine Enzyklopädie zu eponymischen Pflanzennamen |trans-title=Encyclopedia of eponymic plant names | publisher=Botanic Garden and Botanical Museum, Freie Universität Berlin | year=2022 | isbn=978-3-946292-41-8 | url=https://doi.org/10.3372/epolist2022|format=pdf |language=German |location=Berlin | doi=10.3372/epolist2022 | s2cid=246307410 |access-date=January 27, 2022}}</ref>

The genus was [[circumscription (taxonomy)|circumscribed]] by Jean Vincent Félix Lamouroux in Ann. Mus. Natl. Hist. Nat. vol.20 on page 130 in 1813.
It included an initial description of eight species which then subsequently underwent taxonomic revisions.<ref name=":1"/> The genus belongs to order [[Ceramiales]] reported to have 137 species, with a rich body of knowledge spanning for more than 50 years of research.<ref name=":1"/>

''Laurencia'' belongs to the family Rhodomelaceae which is considered to be one of the largest marine red algae family, estimated to have 125 genera and 700 species all over the world. In Laurenciae, a tribe consisting of eight genera, have a taxonomic group called "''Laurencia complex''" or ''Laurencia'' sensu lato which includes six of eight genera, ''[[Chondrophycus]], Laurencia, [[Laurenciella]], [[Osmundea]], [[Palisada]],'' and ''[[Yuzurua]]''.<ref name=":1">{{Citation|last1=Harizani|first1=Maria |date=2016|chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-33172-0_2 |pages=91–252|editor-last=Kinghorn|editor-first=A. Douglas |place=Cham|publisher=Springer International Publishing|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-33172-0_2|isbn=978-3-319-33172-0|access-date=2022-01-23|last2=Ioannou|first2=Efstathia|last3=Roussis|first3=Vassilios|title=Progress in the Chemistry of Organic Natural Products |series=<!-- --> |chapter=The Laurencia Paradox: An Endless Source of Chemodiversity |volume=102|pmid=27380407|editor2-last=Falk|editor2-first=Heinz|editor3-last=Gibbons|editor3-first=Simon|editor4-last=Kobayashi|editor4-first=Jun'ichi|chapter-url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Morphology ==
''Laurencia'' is a small to medium-sized red algae which may appear to be iridescent with thalli reaching up to 40 cm. Thalli can be branching, which can either be bilateral or spread in all directions. Its appendages can be rhizoidal or discoidal in appearance on stoloniferous holdfasts. Branch shape appears to be flat or cylindrical in morphology. Branchlets may be slightly rigid with a shape that may be blunt, truncate or claviform.<ref name=":1"/>

''Laurencia'' has shown high diversity as a genus, with species having distinct features that can easily be determined within the ''Laurencia'' complex.<ref name=":1"/> Molecular studies using rbcL (RuBisCO, Ribulose-1,5-Bisphosphate Carboxylase Oxygenase, Large chain) have uncovered evidences which divided the ''Laurencia'' complex, identifying the genus ''Laurenciella,'' which shares similar morphology with ''Laurencia'' but has a different rbcL sequence.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Saito |first=Yuzuru |date=1967 |title=STUDIES ON JAPANESE SPECIES OF LAURENCIA, WITH SPECIAL REFERENCE TO THEIR COMPARATIVE MORPHOLOGY |url=https://eprints.lib.hokudai.ac.jp/dspace/bitstream/2115/21846/1/15(1)_P1-81.pdf |journal=Memoirs of the Faculty of Fisheries Hokkaido University |language=English}}</ref>

== Distribution ==
''Laurencia'' can be found all over the world, in particular in tropical and subtropical regions with warmer waters.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} Its habitats range from tide pools, reef flats, mud flats, and a variety of hard substrates (e.g. rocks, corals), within intertidal and subtidal zones up to 65 m.<ref name=":1"/>  It is also described as "turf-forming" wherein it can cover a majority of hard substrate in some areas.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}}

In Myanmar, it can be found growing together with some species of ''Cladophora, Chaetomorpha, Dictyota, Gelidium, Ceramium, Caloglossa, Catenella, Polysiphonia, Acanthophora,'' and ''Bostrychia{{citation needed|date=February 2022}}''.

== Ecology ==
''Laurencia'' has numerous ecological roles, serving as refuge for different marine organisms in areas where they grow abundantly, forming forests. They are also hosts of various mircoorganisms and parasitic algae, known as ''Janczewskia''<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Nonomura|first=Arthur M.|date=1979|title=Development of Janczewskia Morimotoi (ceramiales) on Its Host Laurencia Nipponica (ceramiales, Rhodophyceae)1|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1529-8817.1979.tb02979.x|journal=Journal of Phycology|language=en|volume=15|issue=2|pages=154–162|doi=10.1111/j.1529-8817.1979.tb02979.x|s2cid=84862820|issn=1529-8817|url-access=subscription}}</ref>''.'' As producers, they are also fed on by some grazers such as crabs,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kilar|first1=John A.|last2=Lou|first2=Robin M.|date=1984-01-01|title=Ecological and behavioral studies of the decorator crab, Microphrys bicornutus Latreille (Decapoda : Brachyura): A test of optimum foraging theory|url=https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0022-0981%2884%2990083-2|journal=Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology|language=en|volume=74|issue=2|pages=157–167|doi=10.1016/0022-0981(84)90083-2|bibcode=1984JEMBE..74..157K |issn=0022-0981|url-access=subscription}}</ref> queen conch,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=STONER|first1=ALLAN W.|last2=WAITE|first2=JANICE M.|title=Trophic Biology of Strombus Gigas in Nursery Habitats: Diets and Food Sources in Seagrass Meadows|date=1991-11-01|url=https://doi.org/10.1093/mollus/57.4.451|journal=Journal of Molluscan Studies|volume=57|issue=4|pages=451–460|doi=10.1093/mollus/57.4.451|issn=0260-1230|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and sea hares<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wessels|first1=Matthias|last2=König|first2=Gabriele M.|last3=Wright|first3=Anthony D.|date=2000-07-01|title=New Natural Product Isolation and Comparison of the Secondary Metabolite Content of Three Distinct Samples of the Sea Hare Aplysia dactylomela from Tenerife|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/np9905721|journal=Journal of Natural Products|volume=63|issue=7|pages=920–928|doi=10.1021/np9905721|pmid=10924166|bibcode=2000JNAtP..63..920W |issn=0163-3864|url-access=subscription}}</ref> despite its chemical deterrent.

The growth of ''Laurencia'' is significantly affected by changes in nutrient availability and temperature.<ref name=":1"/> The effects of pollution in ''Laurencia'' are somewhat inconsistent showing its adaptability in Indian Ocean but markedly showed a decrease in biomass in polluted areas in the Mediterranean.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Jadeja|first1=R. N.|last2=Tewari|first2=A.|date=February 2011|title=Impact of discharge of soda ash industry effluent on abundance and community structure of rocky intertidal macroalgae of the Arabian Sea, Gujarat, India|url=http://nopr.niscair.res.in/handle/123456789/11373|journal=Indian Journal of Geo-Marine Sciences |volume=40 |issue=1 |pages=71–75 |language=en-US|issn=0975-1033}}</ref> Space within the environment is also a necessity for ''Laurencia'' survival. In field trials, ''Laurencia'' tends to inhibit coral larvae dispersal resulting to higher mortality when the algae is present.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kuffner|first1=Ilsa B.|last2=Walters|first2=Linda J.|last3=Becerro|first3=Mikel A.|last4=Paul|first4=Valerie J.|author4-link=Valerie Paul|last5=Ritson-Williams|first5=Raphael|last6=Beach|first6=Kevin S.|date=2006-10-05|title=Inhibition of coral recruitment by macroalgae and cyanobacteria|url=https://www.int-res.com/abstracts/meps/v323/p107-117/|journal=Marine Ecology Progress Series|language=en|volume=323|pages=107–117|doi=10.3354/meps323107|bibcode=2006MEPS..323..107K|issn=0171-8630|doi-access=free|hdl=10261/132223|hdl-access=free}}</ref>

== Life History ==
''Laurencia'' grows throughout the year, with spermatangial individuals appearing from early August to late September while cystocarpic ones appear from mid-August to late October. From July to October, mature tetrasporangial plants appear.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}} Gametophytic individuals are dioecious in nature, typically developed on the branchlets, but can be present in the main branch as well.<ref name=":1"/>

Male gametophytes contain spermatangia on trichoblast while female gametophytes contain carpogonia, representing the haploid phase. Two diploid phases occur in ''Laurencia'': one with carpogonia and carpospore and the other, with tetrasporangia. Therefore, ''Laurencia'' undergoes three phases in its life cycle: one haploid phase and two diploid phases, consistent to the ''Polysiphonia'' triphasic life history.{{citation needed|date=February 2022}}

== Cultivation and Exploitation ==
A growing interest in the cultivation of ''Laurencia brongniartii'' has emerged due to its potential to be a newfound source for antibiotics.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Nishihara|first1=Gregory N.|last2=Terada|first2=Ryuta|last3=Noro|first3=Tadahide|date=2004-08-01|title=Photosynthesis and growth rates of Laurencia brongniartii J. Agardh (Rhodophyta, Ceramiales) in preparation for cultivation|url=https://doi.org/10.1023/B:JAPH.0000047790.59265.fb|journal=Journal of Applied Phycology|language=en|volume=16|issue=4|pages=303–308|doi=10.1023/B:JAPH.0000047790.59265.fb|bibcode=2004JAPco..16..303N |s2cid=23924692|issn=1573-5176|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The common method is indoor tank culture, utilizing an excised apical tip from a thalli sample. Initial trials have confirmed its viability for culture providing opportunities for personnel with little to no experience in algae cultivation. The cost of production is relatively low, with maintenance costs at its core. Small-scale operations may be profitable in maximizing algae production, however more studies are needed to evaluate these conditions.<ref name=":2"/>

== Chemical Composition ==
''Laurencia'' species are known to have several natural products exhibiting numerous biological activities such as chemical defense against grazers,<ref>{{Cite book|last=Paul|first=Valerie J.|author-link=Valerie Paul|title=Ecological Roles of Marine Natural Products|chapter-url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.7591/9781501737435-005/html|chapter=Chapter 1. Seaweed Chemical Defenses on Coral Reefs|date=2019-05-15|pages=24–50|publisher=Cornell University Press|isbn=978-1-5017-3743-5|language=en|doi=10.7591/9781501737435-005|s2cid=234454451}}</ref> anti-fouling chemical affecting ''Perna perna'' attachment,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Da Gama|first1=Bernardo A P|last2=Pereira|first2=Renato C|last3=Soares|first3=Angélica R|last4=Teixeira|first4=Valéria L|last5=Yoneshigue-Valentin|first5=Yocie|date=2003-01-01|title=Is the Mussel Test a good Indicator of Antifouling Activity? A Comparison Between Laboratory and Field Assays|url=https://doi.org/10.1080/0892701031000089534|journal=Biofouling|volume=19|issue=sup1|pages=161–169|doi=10.1080/0892701031000089534|issn=0892-7014|pmid=14628724|bibcode=2003Biofo..19S.161D |s2cid=19461987|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and anti-fouling activities.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Da Gama|first1=Bernardo A P|last2=Pereira|first2=Renato C|last3=Carvalho|first3=Ana G V|last4=Coutinho|first4=Ricardo|last5=Yoneshigue-Valentin|first5=Yocie|date=2002-01-01|title=The Effects of Seaweed Secondary Metabolites on Biofouling|url=https://doi.org/10.1080/08927010290017680|journal=Biofouling|volume=18|issue=1|pages=13–20|doi=10.1080/08927010290017680|bibcode=2002Biofo..18...13D |s2cid=85850477|issn=0892-7014|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In addition, ''Laurencia'' is known to be an abundant source of halogenated metabolites, including a variety of terpenes (e.g. sesquiterpenes, diterpenes, triterpenes, and C<sub>15</sub> acetogenins).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Suzuki|last2=Vairappan|title=Halogenated secondary metabolites from Japanese species of the red algal genus Laurencia (Rhodomelaceae, Ceramiales)|journal=Current Topics in PhytoChemistry}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=De Nys|first1=R|last2=Leya|first2=T|last3=Maximilien|first3=R|last4=Afsar|first4=A|last5=Nair|first5=P S R|last6=Steinberg|first6=P D|date=1996-09-01|title=The need for standardised broad scale bioassay testing: A case study using the red alga Laurencia rigida|url=https://doi.org/10.1080/08927019609386281|journal=Biofouling|volume=10|issue=1–3|pages=213–224|doi=10.1080/08927019609386281|issn=0892-7014|pmid=22115113|bibcode=1996Biofo..10..213D|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In Vietnam, ''L. snackeyi'' may be a potential species to evaluate new chemical races, similar to ''L. nipponica'' seeing how these may indicate similarities in morphology but differences in chemical content subject to geographical distribution.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tan|first1=Kai Lee|last2=Matsunaga|first2=Shigeki|last3=Vairappan|first3=Charles S.|date=2011|title=Halogenated chamigranes of red alga Laurencia snackeyi (Weber-van Bosse) Masuda from Sulu-Sulawesi Sea|url=https://www.infona.pl//resource/bwmeta1.element.elsevier-e25e464d-0d22-3fa9-96d4-2a7144ae1136|journal=Biochemical Systematics and Ecology|language=English|volume=3|issue=39|pages=213–215|doi=10.1016/j.bse.2010.09.017|bibcode=2011BioSE..39..213L |issn=0305-1978|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Utilization and Management ==
A total of 1047 secondary metabolites have been extracted from ''Laurencia'' and ''Aplysia'' species since 2015. The diverse chemical composition of ''Laurencia'' has been subject to numerous research mainly attributed to both environmental and genetic factors. For years, humans have utilized ''Laurencia'' as food, medicinal products, fertilizers, and from recent research, an abundant source of pharmacological significance.<ref name=":1"/> The commercialization of the species may require further research in order to optimize culture conditions and eventually, harvest greater yield and develop a more systematic cultivation system.<ref name=":2"/>

==Species ==
[[AlgaeBase]], a database with detailed information on species of ''Laurencia'', includes 137 taxonomically accepted species {{as of|2018|lc=y}}, and differentiates these from a further ~375 entries of uncertain taxonomic status; it further delineates homotypic or heterotypic [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonyms]].<ref name="algaebase" />

Commonly observed species of ''Laurencia'' include the shallow [[Neritic zone|subtidal]] ''[[Laurencia nidifica]]'' (Hawaii), ''[[Laurencia pacifica]]'' (California), and ''[[Laurencia thyrsifera]]'' (New Zealand).<ref name=hiln/><ref name=inatobs/> Species seen in the British Isles include ''[[Laurencia hybrida]]'', ''[[Laurencia obtusa]]'', ''[[Laurencia osmunda]]'', ''[[Laurencia pinnatifida]]'', ''[[Laurencia pyramidalis]]'', and ''[[Laurencia truncata]]''.<ref name=Fishes/><ref name=Maggs93/>
